claims.text: Spin-polarized DFT total-energy comparisons can indicate the presence of ferromagnetic ground states in itinerant-electron systems.
Exchange parameters obtained by mapping DFT results onto a Heisenberg model can be used alongside total-energy comparisons to identify ferromagnetic ground states.
The proposed method compares the total energy of a ferromagnetic spin-polarized state with that of a non-spin-polarized state.
The proposed method maps exchange interactions onto a Heisenberg model.
The method is expected to be reliable under low-temperature, well-characterized crystalline conditions when electronic states are accurately described and correlations are moderate.
Positive computed exchange couplings mediate interactions between atomic spins.
A spin-polarized state lower in total energy than the nonmagnetic state indicates energetic preference for magnetic ordering.
Strongly positive mapped exchange parameters indicate that exchange interactions favor parallel spin alignment.
Exchange interactions favoring parallel spin alignment lead to a ferromagnetic ground state.
The ferromagnetic configuration is predicted to have lower total energy than the nonmagnetic configuration.
Positive exchange parameters are predicted to confirm stabilization of the ferromagnetic state.
A non-spin-polarized calculation serves as the reference energy for the comparison.
The method is most reliable for itinerant-electron systems with moderate correlation effects.
The method may be less applicable to highly correlated or localized-electron systems.
DFT approximations and the treatment of electron correlations can introduce uncertainty into calculated energy differences and exchange parameters.
Failure to obtain a lower ferromagnetic energy or consistently positive exchange parameters would falsify the method's prediction of a ferromagnetic ground state.
